title: PeapodCore
description: The twelve core Peapod records. Field names, enums, and defaults are the product contract -- existing client logic and the row-level rules in services/api/src/policy/rls.ts depend on them. Every record carries the four audit columns (id, created_at, updated_at, created_by_id) because the authorization rules are written in terms of created_by_id.

AuditFields.description: Columns present on every record. created_by_id is the owner used by the ownership branch of every row-level policy; it is set server-side from the verified access token and is never accepted from a client payload.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the last mutation.

created_by_id.description: The user who created the row. Server-assigned.

PodGroupType.description: What kind of group this pod is. Drives copy throughout the app (a couple sees different wording than a friend group).

PodRole.description: A member's role in a pod. 'admin' is surfaced in the UI as a 'Seed' -- the only role allowed to rename the pod, generate invite codes, change roles, remove members, or delete the pod.

PlaceAlertEvent.description: Whether the geofence fired on entry or exit.

PlanAudience.description: Who a plan is for. Decides who receives the day-before reminder: 'self' notifies only the creator, 'specific' notifies participant_ids, 'pod' notifies every member.

Pod.description: A pod: the small group that shares location, plans, money, and a world. Everything else in the system is scoped to a pod.

trip_history_enabled.description: When false, members' past movement trails are hidden from the map. A privacy switch owned by the pod admin.

PodMembership.description: Joins a user to a pod with a role. Clients never write this table directly; all changes go through the privileged pod routes so admin checks cannot be bypassed.

PodInvite.description: A short-lived join code. Codes are six characters and expire ten minutes after issue, matching the original behaviour.

User.description: An account. Credentials live in the Python security service; this record holds only the profile fields the app renders.

permissions_granted.description: Set once the user has completed the location + notification onboarding screen. The app shell redirects to that screen while this is false.

role.description: Platform-level role, distinct from PodRole. 'admin' is a Peapod operator, used by the escape hatch in every row-level policy.

LocationPing.description: One GPS fix from one member's device. The highest-volume table in the system: written every time a member moves past the movement threshold, and read in bulk by the compute service to reconstruct trips.

speed.description: Ground speed in metres per second, as reported by the OS.

accuracy.description: Horizontal accuracy radius in metres. Fixes worse than 50 m are discarded during trip reconstruction.

is_driving.description: Device-side guess that this fix was taken in a vehicle.

PhoneStatus.description: Device telemetry shown on a member's card. The *_supported flags exist because some platforms refuse to report battery or connection type, and the UI must show 'N/A' rather than a misleading zero.

FavouritePlace.description: A saved place: home, work, a regular cafe. Doubles as a geofence -- arriving within 150 m creates a PlaceAlert and notifies the pod. A non-null expires_at makes the place temporary (useful for a one-off meeting point).

PlaceAlert.description: An audit trail of geofence crossings. Written by the device that crossed the fence, read to render 'Sarah arrived at Home'.

Plan.description: Anything with a date that is not a full trip: a reminder, a call, a date night. Appears in the unified Plans list alongside trips.

Message.description: A chat message. A null recipient_id makes it a pod-wide group message; a set recipient_id makes it one-to-one. Pod messages are pruned after seven days; direct messages with a null pod_id are retained globally.

Notification.description: An in-app notification addressed to one user. Read/update/delete are restricted to the recipient or the creator.

ImportantDate.description: A pod milestone. count_up dates power 'Together for 1,124 days'; count-down dates power 'Sarah's birthday in 12 days'. The milestone job reads count_up dates to celebrate day 100, 200, 365, 500, 730, and 1000.

date.description: Calendar date, no time component. Parsed as UTC midnight to avoid off-by-one-day errors across time zones.

recurring.description: True for yearly events like birthdays.

pinned.description: The single pinned date is the pod's headline journey, shown on the profile.
